full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J: The above civil petitions for leave to appeal are directed against the judgment and order dated 12.2.2007 of the High Court Division passed in Civil Revision Nos. 3011of 2005 and 4120 of 2006, heard analogously making absolute the Rules and thereby setting aside the judgment and orders dated 8.8.2006 and 27.9.2006 passed by the learned District Judge, Khulna in Civil Revision No.142 of 2005, which arose out of the judgment and order dated 24.9.2007 of the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka passed Miscellaneous Case No.28 of 2005 rejecting the prayer for staying further proceedings of Title Execution Case No.5 of 1993 pending in the same Court. 

 2. Maksudun Nabi Joarder, the petitioner in C.P. No.1388 of 2005, filed the above Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2005 stating that on 20.4.53 Late Golam Nabi Joardar, his predecessor, got settlement of .27 acres of land from the heirs of Nepal Chandra Roy Chowdhury and Aghor Nah Roy Chowdhury, the C.S. recorded tenants, on payment of proper salami and after his death the petitioner along with his co-sharer become the owner of the same and while they were in possession of the same, the defendant respondent Nos. 1 and 2, with some musclemen on 15.2.2005 tried to take over possession of the above land by force which was resisted then and on 16.2.2005 the petitioner filed Petition Case No. 66 of 2005 in the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Khulna under section 145 Cr. P.C. wherein the respondents Nos. 1 and 2 on 28.2.2005 filed written objection stating that they obtaining decree in Title Suit No.94 of 1990 in respect of the above land became owner of the same and then on obtaining the certified copy of suit register on 10.3.2005 the petitioner came to know that by suppressing summons the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 obtained a decree on 21.8.1997 exparte declaring their title in the above land and though the petitioner was made a party in the above suit as defendant No.2, the summons issued 1 against him was suppressed and further Hormuja Begum and Hosne Ara Joardar, respectively the wife and daughter of Golam Nabi Joardar, who are the petitioners in C.P. No. 454 of 2008, were not made parties in the above suit and since the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 were trying to take possession of the suit land through Title Execution Case No.5 of 1993 the petitioner filed the above miscellaneous and on 13.3.2005, also filed an application therein praying for stay of further proceedings of the above title execution case till disposal of the above  miscellaneous case. After hearing, the learned Joint District Judge rejected the prayer for stay. The petitioner then preferred Civil Revision No. 34 of 2005 and after hearing, the learned District Judge made the Rule absolute and stayed further proceeding of Title Execution Case No.5 of 1993. 

 3. The above wife and daughter of late Golam Nabi Joardar also filed Title Suit No.85 of 2005 in the same very Court of the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka seeking declaration that the above exparte decree dated 21.8.1993 passed in Title Suit No. 94 of 1990 is fraudulent, collusive, illegal and not binding upon them and in the said suit they by application dated 13.9.2005 prayed for temporary injunction for restraining the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 from entering into possession of the suit land and by order dated 13.9.2005 the parties were directed to maintain status quo with respect to the suit land but in October, 2005, the respondents Nos.1 and 2, disregarding the order of status-quo, tried to get possession of the suit land through Title Execution Case No.5 of 1993 and finding no other alternative they on 20.10.2005, filed an application in Title Execution Case No.5 of 1993 praying for stay of further proceedings of the execution case and the learned Joint District Judge having rejected the above prayer for stay by order dated 17.11.2005, they preferred Civil Revision No.142 of 2005 and the learned District Judge, Khulna by order dated 17.11.2005 adjourned hearing till 27.9.2006 and then by order dated 27.9.2006 adjourned hearing till disposal of . Civil Revision No.3011 of 2005 and as against that the respondents No.1 and 2 moved the High Court Division obtained Rule in Civil Revision No.4120 of 2006. 

 4. The High Court Division, after hearing the Civil Revision Nos. 3011 of 2005 and 4120 of 2006 analogously, made both the roles absolute on the findings that pendency of the above Miscellaneous Case No.28 of 2005, which has been filed 13 years after the decree, is not a good ground for stay of execution. 

 5. The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the High Court Division fell in error in not considering that the exparte decree sought to be executed is one for recovery of possession and the petitioner has filed the above Miscellaneous Case No.28 of 2005 under Order 9 Rule 1 on the allegation that summon of the suit was not served upon him and the above miscellaneous case being ready for hearing the High Court Division ought to have directed the Court below to dispose of the miscellaneous case within a certain time and the High Court Division also failed to consider that the petitioners of C.P. No. 454 of 2005 being not made a party in the above Title Suit No. 94 of 1990, the exparte decree dated 21.8.1993 passed there is not binding upon them and they filing Title Suit No.85 of 2005 challenged the above exparte decree and also obtained an order in Civil Revision No.142 of 2005 directing the parties to maintain status quo with respect to the suit land and if the execution case is allowed to proceed   the same will amount to violation of the order of status quo and that Rule was issued in Civil Revision No.4120 of 2006 to consider legality of order 8.8.2006 and 27.9.2006 by which the learned District Judge had adjourned hearing of Civil Revision No.4120 of 2006 and the High Court Division without deciding the fate and future of the above Civil Revision No. 4120 of 2006 made the rule absolute observing that the execution case shall proceed. 

 6. As it appears the High Court Division discharged the Rules Holding that the teamed District Judge has allowed the prayer for stay of further proceeding of Title Execution Case No. 5 of 1993 merely on the ground that the above Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2005 has been instituted on 12.03.2005 i.e. long after 13 years after passing of the exparte decree passed in Title Suit No. 94 of 1990 and therefore the pendency of the above miscellaneous case can not be a good ground to stay the execution case which the respondent Nos. 12 have obtained before 13 years and furthermore, there is no certainty that the above miscellaneous case will be disposed of within certain date and so the respondent Nos. 1 and 2, the decree holder, can not wait for uncertain period and therefore the learned District Judge fell in error in not appreciating that a decree holder can not be debarred from executing the decree for an indefinite period.
